data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The book has 300 pages, but a verification via simulation of the digit-counting function confirms that D(300) = 792 and D(299) = 789, D(301) = 795, establishing 300 as the unique solution.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If D(n) is not strictly monotonic (e.g., if some pages have zero digits), uniqueness may fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 792 is not in the range of D for any valid n (which it is, since D(300)=792), there would be no solution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The digit-counting function D(n) = \u03a3_{k=1}^{n} len(str(k)) is strictly increasing for n \u2265 1, since each additional page adds at least one digit. Therefore, if D(n) = 792 has a solution, it is unique. Computing: D(299) = 9 + 180 + 3\u00d7200 = 789; D(300) = 789 + 3 = 792; D(301) = 792 + 3 = 795. The unique n with D(n) = 792 is n = 300. The causal mechanism is the monotonicity of cumulative digit count with respect to page count.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
